sentences.text: ?Court No. - 8

Case :- U/S 482/378/407 No. - 2219 of 2020
Applicant :- Rambali

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. & Anr.
Counsel for Applicant :- Sunil Kumar Singh,Vivek Kumar Divedi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Virendra Kumar-II,J.
Heard Shri Sunil Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned A.G.A. for the State, who participated in the proceedings through video conferencing.

Petitioner has assailed impugned summoning order dated 24.01.2020 passed by the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate(First), Hardoi in Complaint Case No. 597 of 2020, under Section 26(2)(i) 59(i) of Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006, P.S. Arval, District Hardoi.

A complaint has been filed by the Food Safety Officer, in which it is narrated that on 02.05.2017 at about 4:20 p.m. in Jassapurwa, District Hardoi the Food Safety Officer inspected the premises/
shop of the petitioner and took samples of ice candy liquid, which was sent for chemical analysis to the Public Analyst, U.P., Agra which was found to be substandard and unsafe as per Section 3(1)(zzz)(v) of F.S.S. Act, 2006.
Saccharine sodium was present in the sample.
On the basis of complaint filed by the Food Safety Officer the trial court has summoned the petitioner vide impugned order dated 24.01.2020.

Learned counsel for petitioner has submitted that the Food Safety Officer has filed a false complaint against the petitioner and no opportunity was given to the petitioner to contradict the report submitted by the Public Analyst of the Laboratory at Agra.
In these circumstances, proceedings of complaint is liable to be quashed.

sentences.text:
Learned A.G.A. has submitted that Food Safety Officer, after inspection of premises/ shop of petitioner found that ice candy liquid was found substandard as per the report of Public Analyst,
therefore, proceedings of complaint case are not liable to be quashed.
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, prima facie involvement of petitioner is apparent on the basis of facts narrated in the complaint made by the Food Safety Officer.
There is no ground for interference by invoking powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
The petition lacks merit and is liable to be dismissed.
Dismissed Accordingly.
At this stage, learned counsel for petitioner has lastly submitted that some time may be granted to the petitioner to appear and surrender before the concerned trial court.

In view of above, it is provided that if petitioner surrenders and appear before the trial court within 15 days from today and moves application for bail, his bail application shall be decided expeditiously in accordance with the exposition of law of this Court as well as of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
For the aforesaid period of 15 days no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioner.
It is made clear that the aforesaid period of 15 days shall not be extended in any circumstance.
With the above observations/ directions, the present petition is dismissed.
Order Date :- 8.10.2020 Mustaqeem  Rambali vs State Of U.P. & Anr. on 8 October, 2020
